title: You can't remember being a baby — and your brain wiped it
voiceover: You can't remember being a baby. And it's not because nothing happened. It's because your brain was actively deleting everything. The part of your brain that stores long-term memories, the hippocampus, isn't fully developed until you're around three or four. Before that, you form memories — but your brain has no way to file them. Even weirder: scientists think rapid neuron growth in babies actively erases old memories to make room for new connections. So somewhere in there, you had a favorite toy, a first word, a real personality. And your own brain wiped it all. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
